headline: Meta is claiming billions of dollars in US research tax credits by treating its AI data centers as experimental projects, the New York Times reported.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 to 3: a repeat of the New York Times report of 30 Sep, already in our 1 Oct edition, with no new development.
importance_line: If the method holds, other large AI spenders could copy it and the US Treasury would lose revenue, but the IRS could still challenge it and Meta says it follows rules set by Congress.
summary: The New York Times reported on 30 Sep 2026, as relayed by ET Datacenters, that Meta cut its tax bill by 2 billion dollars in 2024 and expects to save 3.9 billion in 2025 by describing its AI data centers in tax filings as "pilot models" to claim a research tax credit. Meta says it uses incentives Congress set for domestic investment but declined to say what makes the data centers experimental, and the former congressman who sponsored the credit says Meta's use goes "way, way beyond" what anyone imagined; we carried this report on 1 Oct.
notes: Old news (30 Sep) repeated by ET Datacenters on 10 Oct; no new development. Held back by the repeat rule if the main session applies it.
